content.overview: A result becomes operational evidence only when it is reviewed, linked to the correct lot and transferred with its limitations and status. The handoff should not imply authority the reviewer does not possess.

vocabulary.definition: Qualified evaluation of analytical report completeness, method context and result validity.
Controlled evaluation of identity, records, specifications, deviations and decision readiness.
Traceable history of creation, change, review and status actions.

sections.title: Review identity and completeness
sections.body: The handoff should show that sample, lot, report version, dates, panel and required qualifiers were checked.

sections.title: Preserve questions and exceptions
sections.body: Missing information, amended reports, sample deviations and unresolved interpretation should remain explicit.

sections.title: Transfer status and authority
sections.body: The receiving role needs current lot status, allowed actions, decision owner and next step. Written plus verbal handoff is appropriate when risk is material.

workedExamples: A specialist completes report review but leaves disposition pending because a sample-identity discrepancy requires authorized quality resolution.
commonMistakes: Treating receipt of a COA as completed review.
Marking a lot released without decision authority.
content.practicalApplication: Build a result-review cover sheet linking lot genealogy, chain of custody, report version, checks, exceptions, status and owner.
content.summary: Laboratory evidence supports decisions only when identity, review, exceptions and authority remain connected.
